prevents: Interview duration cannot be computed from the paper form at all -- it has no start-time field, only 7.01 end time. This is the exact signal that identified the 94-interview, 4-minute-mean fraud case, but only after fieldwork closed.
source_or_judgement: My judgement, directly driven by the operating-conditions fraud case

rule_added: ODK deviceid metadata captured automatically
prevents: Cannot attribute submissions to a specific tablet for the per-device duplicate-label check (requirement 8) or for device-level QA dashboards
source_or_judgement: My judgement

prevents: Non-numeric or >3-digit entry that cannot fit the printed 3-digit box
source_or_judgement: Paper form coding box is three digits wide (⌷⌷⌷); my judgement on the implied range

prevents: Non-numeric or >3-digit entry

rule_added: team_code_display = pulldata('staff_roster', 'team_code', 'name', enumerator_code), shown read-only; the enumerator never types a team code
prevents: Paper 1.09 lets an enumerator enter their own code correctly at 1.08 but a mistyped or wrong team code at 1.09, which would then misassign the specimen-label range check in Section 5 to the wrong team's block
source_or_judgement: Derived from staff_roster.csv (120 rows, 24 teams, verified 1:1 with specimen_label_allocation.csv team codes)

rule_added: 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-30 (closed interval)
prevents: Backdated/postdated entries; device clock errors; typed year defaulting to device-current-year instead of 2026
source_or_judgement: Printed on the questionnaire header ('Fieldwork period 1 to 30 June 2026'). NOTE: this conflicts with the operating-conditions brief, which states fieldwork runs 14 days -- flagged as defect D-07, escalated, not resolved silently. I used the form's own printed period because it is the ethics-approved text.

rule_added: longitude 6.3-9.0, latitude 10.0-11.9 (geopoint bounding box)
prevents: Wrong-hemisphere entry, transposed lat/long, GPS fix taken indoors far from the dwelling, stale cached fix from a previous survey
source_or_judgement: My judgement -- padded from the settlement register's actual coordinate extent (longitude 6.9544 to 8.4288, latitude 10.3659 to 11.5735 across the 2,524 settlements in settlements.csv) with roughly a 0.4-0.5 degree margin for genuine edge-of-catchment points

rule_added: regex ^BAN-[0-9]{6}$, and must resolve via pulldata() against previous_round_households.csv (3,982 rows, format verified 100% compliant)
prevents: A transcription error that silently creates a phantom link between this round and a household that was never actually visited last round, which would corrupt any longitudinal linkage analysis
source_or_judgement: previous_round_households.csv, all 3,982 household_id values checked; format is uniform

prevents: Zero or absurd entries (e.g. 300 from a stuck key); still permits genuinely large compound households up to 30
source_or_judgement: My judgement -- no household-size distribution was supplied in the data pack for Bansara state, so I set a generous ceiling rather than infer one

rule_added: select_one yes/no gates which of age_years / age_months is asked
prevents: The paper form leaves it to the enumerator's judgement which of columns (5)/(6) to fill for a borderline-looking child, which a printed form can get away with but a digital form's relevant logic cannot -- it needs an explicit branch
source_or_judgement: My judgement

prevents: A member coded 'not under five' with an age below 5, or an implausible age from a stuck key (e.g. 999)
source_or_judgement: Lower bound follows directly from the routing question; upper bound is my judgement (no Bansara demographic data supplied)

prevents: A member coded 'under five' with a months value that is actually five years or older, which would silently misroute Section 4/5 eligibility
source_or_judgement: Definitional: 'under five years' cannot exceed 59 completed months

rule_added: Split into weight_status (measured/not measured/refused) + c_weight_kg numeric 2.0-30.0, numeric field only relevant if status=measured
prevents: The paper form's '99 = not measured' sentinel living inside a continuous kg field, which is analytically indistinguishable from a genuine (if unlikely) 99.0kg entry once digitised as a plain decimal field
source_or_judgement: Range is my judgement, generously padded around WHO Child Growth Standards weight-for-age for 9-59 months to avoid rejecting true severe-malnutrition or high-BMI outliers while catching entry blunders (e.g. a misplaced decimal point)

rule_added: Recorded alongside height so the office can apply the standard 0.7cm recumbent/standing correction; a mid-survey change in which position is used for a given age band is expected (operating conditions say a measurement-position change is likely mid-round) and must not be blocked
prevents: A position switch is a real, expected event this round -- flagging it (via the codebook, not a form constraint) is correct; refusing it in-form is not
source_or_judgement: Operating conditions: 'A change to the instrument part way through the round is likely'

rule_added: Split into height_status + c_height_cm numeric 45.0-130.0, only relevant if status=measured
prevents: Same collision as weight: paper's '99 = not measured' inside a 3-digit continuous cm field
source_or_judgement: Range is my judgement, padded around WHO length/height-for-age for 9-59 months

rule_added: measles_status combines card-confirmed and recall answers into one analysis field, but the raw vacc_card_seen/measles_from_card/measles_recall fields are kept, not overwritten
prevents: Analysts silently losing the card-confirmed-vs-recall distinction, which Q4 of this same assessment explicitly requires reporting on for coverage
source_or_judgement: My judgement, informed by the Q4 requirement to report coverage 'by documented source, distinguishing card confirmed from caregiver recall'

rule_added: select_one backed by an internal XLSForm choices list (medicine_list, 14 rows), an illustrative WHO-AWaRe-informed list of 13 common oral/injectable antibiotics + Other(96), every label prefixed [PLACEHOLDER]
prevents: A blocked or fabricated-looking field where the real ministry-approved antimicrobial code list should be
source_or_judgement: ESCALATED, not resolved: the questionnaire refers to 'the medicine list' but reference_media/ contains no such file. This is a data-pack gap, not something I can responsibly invent an authoritative version of. The placeholder must be replaced by the ministry/AMR technical working group's actual formulary code list before deployment.

rule_added: 'new' forces the camera to open for a fresh capture; the device's photo gallery is not offered as a source
prevents: An enumerator attaching an old or unrelated photo from the gallery instead of actually photographing this packaging, which would defeat the evidence purpose of the field entirely
source_or_judgement: My judgement

rule_added: image capture attached whenever antibiotic_photo=1 (photo taken)
prevents: The paper form records only whether a photo was taken, not the photo itself, so the office has no way to verify the antibiotic_code entry against the packaging -- an AMR-survey-specific back-office QA gap
source_or_judgement: My judgement

rule_added: Section only shown when age_months>=12 (already on file); no separate 5.01 question is asked
prevents: 5.01 restates a fact already captured at 4.03/age_months two questions earlier; asking it again lets an enumerator answer 'yes, >=12 months' for a child whose age_months says 10, an internal contradiction the paper form has no mechanism to prevent
source_or_judgement: My judgement -- resolved in form, disclosed in defects report D-04, not silently dropped

rule_added: regex ^BSN[0-9]{6}-[0-9X]$; 6-digit body inside the enumerator's own team range (pulldata from specimen_label_allocation.csv); check character recomputed via modulus-11, weights 2-7 right to left, and compared to the entered character; must not repeat within this same household's roster (count of matching labels across all roster/specimen/specimen_label nodes in this submission <= 1)
prevents: Mistyped labels, a label affixed and typed from outside the team's allocated block (allocation confirmed contiguous, no gaps/overlaps across 24 teams x 900 labels each, 480000-501599), transposed-digit-pair errors the check digit is specifically designed to catch, and the same physical label being typed twice for two different children in the same household
source_or_judgement: specimen_label_allocation.csv (24 rows) for the range; check-digit scheme text in that same file ('Modulus 11, weights 2 to 7 applied right to left, remainder 10 recorded as X'). See documentation/04_specimen_label_validation.md for worked test vectors, and documentation/05_duplicate_label_detection.md for why a same-submission check only catches labels reused within one household and not the full 9-day device history.

rule_added: An earlier build set appearance='numbers' on this field, which restricts the on-screen keyboard to digits only. This field's own format is BSN######-C -- letters and an occasional 'X' check character -- so a numeric-only keypad would have made a correctly formatted label untypeable. No appearance is set now; the default keyboard accepts the full alphanumeric format.
prevents: A numeric keypad blocking entry of a field whose own required format includes letters
source_or_judgement: Caught on review while adding appearances for this update, not by a field test -- flagged here anyway since it is exactly the kind of thing device testing (documentation/11_scope_and_omissions.md, item 9) is meant to catch

rule_added: 0.0-12.0 degrees C
prevents: Miskeyed or unrealistic cold-chain temperatures (e.g. a stuck '99', or a positive-but-implausible double-digit reading)
source_or_judgement: My judgement -- WHO cold-chain guidance targets 2-8C for specimen transport; I padded to 0-12C to admit a plausible faulty-but-real thermometer reading rather than only the ideal range, while still rejecting clear entry errors

rule_added: roster_count_actual = count(roster); roster_mismatch_flag=1 when it differs from hh_size_stated; enumerator sees an on-screen note and must actively continue past it, but the form is not blocked
prevents: A genuine mismatch between the pre-roster estimate (3.01) and the actual listed count is real, common (memory, definitional disputes about who is 'usually resident'), and analytically important -- it must reach the office for review, not be silently forced to agree or hard-blocked in the field
source_or_judgement: Q3 requirement 4: 'at minimum reconcile the stated household size against the roster'

rule_added: Not a validation rule: the child module is nested inside each roster row and shown if and only if that row is age-eligible, so the count of completed child modules and the count of eligible roster rows are the same value by construction. 3.02 itself is no longer asked -- see D-01.
prevents: The paper's separate manual count (3.02) and separate manual line-number re-entry (4.01) were themselves the source of the mismatch risk this requirement exists to catch
source_or_judgement: Q3 requirement 4: 'the stated number of eligible children against the number of child modules completed'

rule_added: selected('H') implies count-selected=1 (None of these excludes every other option)
prevents: A response set that includes both 'None of these' and a specific asset (e.g. mobile telephone), which is self-contradictory and breaks any asset-index construction downstream
source_or_judgement: The paper form is a 'select all that apply' multi-select with no stated exclusivity rule for its own 'None of these' category -- identified as defect D-09 (data that cannot be analysed as printed), resolved in form

rule_added: duration_minutes = (end - start) in minutes, computed from the system start/end metadata rather than the enumerator typing a clock time
prevents: The manually-typed 7.01 time can be edited/guessed by an enumerator wanting to disguise a short interview; the system timestamp cannot
source_or_judgement: Directly answers Q3 requirement 11 (fabrication detection) using the operating-conditions fraud case as the design driver
